intent: Compare merge-base..HEAD changed files against a declared CBSP21/RPMCC24 scope manifest. Fail loud when the check cannot be performed.

acceptance.behavior: A changed file that is declared in scope produces no contamination finding.
A changed file not declared in scope produces a contamination finding.
A pinned base that differs from the actual merge-base produces a base-drift finding.
Declared-scope coverage below 95% produces the summary/high-severity result.
A clean, fully covered scope produces zero findings.
Ordinary scans without review context remain silent (no findings).
Missing manifest, unresolved merge-base, shallow-clone failure, or failed git diff must fail loud — never return an empty pass.

A manifest with wrong-typed or out-of-range fields (non-numeric min_coverage_percent, non-object scope/diff_range, non-string pinned_merge_base) yields a CRITICAL uncheckable finding of kind 'malformed_manifest'. An exception escaping run() would abort the scan, which is the silent pass this detector exists to prevent.

A manifest whose schema_version is not 'cbsp21_patch_manifest_v2' is rejected (kind 'schema_version_mismatch'). A v1 manifest carries no pinned_merge_base, so the base-drift check would silently no-op and the scan would look clean for the wrong reason.
A manifest declaring neither paths_in_scope nor files_expected_to_change yields kind 'empty_declared_scope' rather than flagging every changed file.
scope.min_coverage_percent may raise the threshold above 95 but never below it. A manifest must not be able to opt itself out of the coverage_below_95 criterion.

The coverage finding distinguishes scope coverage (share of the real diff that was declared) from file_context_coverage_percent (author's declared review depth) and reports which tripped via metadata.triggered_by.

When diff_range.base is absent, the pinned merge-base is used as the diff base. Falling back to 'HEAD' would make `git merge-base HEAD HEAD` resolve to HEAD, producing an empty changed set and a silent clean pass.
Fingerprints exclude live percentages and SHAs so the same problem keeps one identity across runs; volatile detail stays in the message and metadata.
